requirements:
R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with rustc --edition 2024, std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. Do not use inner attributes or inner doc comments.
R2. Expose these public operations and types, with the listed derives: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Alphabet { Standard, Hex } #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Padding { Required, Omitted } pub fn encode(input: &[u8], alphabet: Alphabet, padding: Padding) -> String; pub fn decode(input: &str, alphabet: Alphabet, padding: Padding) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DecodeError>; #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum DecodeError { InvalidByte { offset: usize, byte: u8 }, Padding { offset: usize }, InvalidLength { offset: usize }, TrailingBits { offset: usize } }
R3. Alphabet::Standard has values 0..31 given by ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567.
R4. Alphabet::Hex has values 0..31 given by 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV. Alphabets never autodetect or blend.
R5. Both alphabets are uppercase only. Lowercase, whitespace, hyphens, and non-ASCII are invalid.
R6. Encoding reads each byte most significant bit first, emits successive five-bit alphabet values, and zero-fills the right of the final partial value.
R7. Padding::Required appends = to a multiple of eight symbols; full blocks get none.
R8. Padding::Omitted never emits =. It does not otherwise change symbols or zero-fill.
R9. Both modes encode empty bytes to an empty string and decode an empty string to an empty vector.
R10. Decoding validates in this strict order: all lexical bytes, mode/placement of padding, data length, padding shape, unused bits. Return only the earliest error from the earliest failing pass.
R11. Lexical validation scans all original UTF-8 bytes left to right. The first byte outside the selected alphabet and = gives InvalidByte { offset, byte }. Even Omitted treats = as lexically recognized and checks it in the next pass.
R12. Every error offset is zero-based in original UTF-8 bytes. InvalidByte carries the actual byte, so a non-ASCII character fails on its first UTF-8 byte.
R13. Let n be input byte length and p the first = offset, or n if absent. In Omitted mode, any = gives Padding { offset: p }, after the complete lexical pass but before data-length validation.
R14. In Required mode, the first alphabet byte after p gives Padding at that byte. This precedes data-length validation.
R15. Let d=p after padding placement. Legal d modulo 8 residues are 0,2,4,5,7. Any other residue gives InvalidLength { offset: n } in either mode.
R16. In Required mode, residues 0,2,4,5,7 need respectively exactly 0,6,4,3,1 copies of =, and total length divisible by eight.
R17. Wrong Required padding shape gives Padding { offset: p }, including p=n when padding is missing. Even all-padding strings and padding after a complete data block are errors.
R18. In Omitted mode, every legal data length is accepted without a total-length divisibility requirement; padding shape has no further check.
R19. Decode data most significant bit first; padding contributes no bits.
R20. Unused low bits must be zero: data residue 2 requires 2 zero bits, 4 requires 4, 5 requires 1, 7 requires 3; residue 0 has none.
R21. Nonzero unused bits give TrailingBits { offset: d-1 }, only after all earlier checks succeed, in both modes.
R22. Errors return no partial byte vector; successive calls are independent.
R23. Support arbitrary bytes and repeated blocks. For every successful decode, re-encoding with the same alphabet and padding reproduces the original string.
R24. The enum choices must apply per call; changing alphabet or padding on one call must not influence later calls.
